title: Logical implication audit of 21 raw semantic proposals
scope: Tests whether each mechanism entails its proposed observation; no manuscript result or gold role is inferred.

entries.implication: A reset mechanism predicts a post-boundary change only if owner/item cues are observable and the interruption is the causal boundary.
entries.assumptions: Requires independent cues and matched boundaries; DIC001's reset likeness alone is insufficient.
entries.countermodel: A drawing interruption can correlate with page layout while state continues, so null change does not refute all reset semantics.

entries.implication: Nonreset continuity predicts cross-line owner persistence only when line pairs share a record and no unobserved topic shift intervenes.
entries.assumptions: Requires independent records, owners, and interruption status.
entries.countermodel: A semantic boundary may coincide with an ordinary line break; a break penalty would challenge this model but not all non-clausal line uses.

entries.implication: A handoff mechanism predicts an edge-specific role interaction only if register transitions and roles are independently identified.
entries.assumptions: The effect must exceed section, host, and position composition.
entries.countermodel: A whole can have a register-conditioned role without being a handoff marker; no interaction weakens this edge model only.

entries.implication: Locus-attached meaning predicts some cross-reading stability, but not identical surface association under transcription errors or allomorphy.
entries.assumptions: Requires correct raw-locus joins, reading error model, and adequate support per register.
entries.countermodel: A true meaning can fail the two-of-three rule when decisive loci are lost or sparse; failure tests reading robustness, not meaning generally.

entries.implication: A role with genuine incompatibility predicts fewer incompatible slots only if the slot ontology is independently valid.
entries.assumptions: Compatibility cannot be defined from the candidate outcome.
entries.countermodel: A broad role may occur in both slots through polysemy or context; violations refute the narrow exclusivity claim, not the role family.

entries.implication: Reciprocal frame compatibility follows from context-free interchangeability, not from merely sharing a broad semantic family.
entries.assumptions: Requires enough independent frames in both directions and a transcription-error model.
entries.countermodel: A general form and a specialized allomorph can share meaning with one-way frame inclusion; failed reciprocity rejects equality, not shared role.

entries.implication: A-B-A referent return predicts owner/slot continuity between the two A positions only if B is a bounded intervention.
entries.assumptions: A positions need independent referent adjudication and controls for template recurrence.
entries.countermodel: Repeated A can be a formula with changing referent; continuity failure challenges return semantics, not recurrence itself.

entries.implication: An indexical label mechanism predicts same-panel owner transfer only where a singular native connector exists.
entries.assumptions: Proximity and generic class codes must be independently separated.
entries.countermodel: A label may denote a reusable class while sharing a panel; failed owner transfer rejects pointer use for that occurrence class.

entries.implication: An operator role predicts action/result framing only if action and result are real independent categories; it does not entail a result within a fixed distance.
entries.assumptions: The proposal must avoid assuming visible result markers or a universal latency.
entries.countermodel: An operator can license an implicit, delayed, or cross-record result, so local framing failure does not refute operator semantics generally.

entries.implication: Measured-entity attachment predicts directional amount adjacency only if amount direction and material/operation slots are independently known.
entries.assumptions: Side and slot labels cannot be inferred from the candidate whole.
entries.countermodel: A material can be implicit or an operation can share the same slot; failed direction rejects the narrow attachment model, not all quantity semantics.

entries.implication: A state-change role predicts directional association with independently tagged quality transitions, not merely co-occurrence near dry/moist forms.
entries.assumptions: Quality tags and held paths must be independent of the candidate.
entries.countermodel: A material name can be reused across transitions; absent direction challenges state-change interpretation only.

entries.implication: Topic introduction predicts later owner continuity only if record boundaries and topic shifts are independently visible.
entries.assumptions: Position alone cannot define an initial topic.
entries.countermodel: An opener may introduce no topic, or topic can shift silently; continuity failure does not refute all record-level organization.

entries.implication: An operation need not produce a visible result within two fields; the mechanism entails a result relation only at whatever scope the process model specifies.
entries.assumptions: A latency bound requires an independent process theory or preregistration, not intuition.
entries.countermodel: Delayed, implicit, or externally represented results make the two-field threshold a test-design failure rather than a semantic falsifier.

entries.implication: A one-to-one amount-to-entity prediction follows only for a unitary measurement grammar with one selected entity per frame.
entries.assumptions: Mixed amounts, shared materials, and implicit entities must be modeled first.
entries.countermodel: A valid amount frame can quantify a mixture or coordinated entities; duplicate/zero attachments then do not refute quantity semantics.

entries.implication: A material-part meaning predicts concentration only if the record system repeatedly names one part and the candidate is not a broad material class.
entries.assumptions: Independent part captions and comparable opportunity counts are required.
entries.countermodel: A material can legitimately occur across several parts; diffuse concentration rejects a narrow one-part claim, not material meaning.

entries.implication: A closure role predicts reduced post-closure action only when record release and action boundaries are independently defined.
entries.assumptions: Terminal position cannot substitute for a boundary binding.
entries.countermodel: Closure may release one subroutine while another action continues; subsequent action does not automatically refute closure semantics.

entries.implication: Definite/anaphoric switching predicts different cue rates after prior mention only if owner identity and introduction cues are independently annotated.
entries.assumptions: Repeated forms must not be assumed to repeat referents.
entries.countermodel: A fixed lexical item can recur with or without cues; failure challenges article-like switching, not reference generally.

entries.implication: Source-before-target order follows an ordered-argument mechanism, but only if source and target roles are independently defined.
entries.assumptions: Layout order, omitted arguments, and reversible operations need explicit alternatives.
entries.countermodel: A valid operation may allow target-first or implicit source; reversal does not universally refute action semantics.

entries.implication: Next-head scope predicts local compatibility only if heads and modifier boundaries are independently tagged.
entries.assumptions: Interrupted and nested scope must be represented rather than forced into one-head frames.
entries.countermodel: A modifier can scope over a phrase or backward; next-head failure rejects the one-head hypothesis only.

entries.implication: Record-initial deixis predicts native-source resolution only when a singular connector exists and the initial form is not a generic opener.
entries.assumptions: Proximity-only ownership is insufficient.
entries.countermodel: An initial form can be deictic to a nonvisible or inherited source; failed visible resolution limits this implementation, not all deixis.

entries.implication: A unit role predicts cross-material recurrence in one measure slot only if materials and units are independently identified.
entries.assumptions: The recurrence threshold must account for opportunity and register.
entries.countermodel: A material class can recur with several materials or a unit can alternate slots; failure rejects the narrow invariant-unit model, not measurement semantics.
